behavior: Settings selects a public HTTPS anisette v3 origin explicitly. Production lazily constructs its existing transport and Keychain owners only when an actual account action requires them; no default remote provider or startup connection.

Actual client_info, provisioning WebSocket, Apple lookup/start/finish and get_headers use bounded messages and an explicit deadline with cancellation and worker drain. No Apple ID/password/token is sent to the provider.
A stable logical protocol identifier and provisioning intent are persisted before remote mutation; accepted adi_pb is persisted before use. Unknown results refuse automatic replay.

Settings shows only registration phase. An explicit confirmed reset signs out stored Apple credentials with accurate readback before changing an unknown logical identity; interrupted retries retain one proposed identity and never delete a provisioned blob.

Explicit protected PKCS12 plus allowlisted public JSON import an actual SecIdentity into the same App Keychain. Exact host certificate, private-key challenge, offline root chain and genuine persistent reference are verified before same-Document publication.

Pairing import preserves the signing namespace and trust anchors, refuses active or unknown transactions, keeps old identities, and uses existing reload behavior after a lost durable ACK. Cancellation waits for the actual importer and observations to finish.
The Settings command result comes from its exact operation. Busy or failed operations cannot display successful import or overwrite an edited service draft through an unrelated nil owner problem.
